headline: Across five sweeps on 2026-08-09 the day's decisive addition remains USDA's July circular cutting French maize 24% to 10.0 Mt, but this fifth run adds the distribution behind the UK number - 90% of AHDB's survey farms below their own five-year wheat average, in the earliest barley harvest since records began in 2006 - brings Cameroon into the corpus at 247,914 t of cocoa, down 19.9%, and corrects a contradiction that four earlier logs had repeated: the two AHDB winter wheat condition readings are consecutive, not conflicting, and that series is now charting.
key_points: FIFTH SWEEP OF 2026-08-09, and the third in the day to find run_state.window_end already equal to today. Window re-covered unchanged at 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-09 (14 days); run_state was not moved. All 21 manifest sources had been checked by one of the four earlier runs, so this run targeted what none of them had mined: the AHDB harvest report in detail, West African cocoa on the ground, Brazilian coffee weather, and the Texas flood follow-up.

AHDB'S FIRST HARVEST REPORT WAS ONLY HALF MINED. Earlier runs took the four headline yields. The report also carries the harvest-progress series and the distribution: 90% of the 60-farm survey sample came in below their own five-year average for winter wheat, with only 10% above, and farm reports spanning 3.9 to 11.5 t/ha. Winter barley was 95% cut by 26 July, the earliest harvest since AHDB records began in 2006; wheat 54%, oilseed rape 73% (Scotland only 8%), spring barley 8%.

POSITIVE, AND THE DROUGHT'S ONE GIFT: GB wheat quality is exceptional. Group 1 specific weights range 76-85 kg/hl and protein averages 13.5%, with samples above 14% described as not uncommon. Low tonnage, high concentration is the classic dry-season trade-off and it partly offsets the loss for milling growers.

CAMEROON ENTERS THE CORPUS AND IT IS THE LARGEST UNREPORTED COCOA NUMBER OF THE WEEK. Marketed production for 2025/26 fell 19.9% to 247,914 tonnes, the weakest in five seasons, with exports down 34.7% to 125,469 tonnes. Both rows carry a review_flag: the source ties adverse West African weather to the 2026/27 outlook, not explicitly to this decline, so the hazard attribution is inferred from regional context while the figures themselves are exact and quoted.

WEST AFRICAN COCOA IS NOW TWO OPPOSITE PROBLEMS IN ADJACENT COUNTRIES. Ghana faces more rain on a crop already damaged by excessive rain, disease and weak pod development, with Western and Western North worst hit by low cherelle counts; Cote d'Ivoire's main crop needs more sunshine after cool, cloudy conditions. Moisture is adequate on both sides of the border and insolation is not. New York September cocoa settled at $5,776/t, down 1.80%, on better Ghanaian supply news.

BRAZIL COFFEE: A LARGE CROP IS NOT THE SAME AS AVAILABLE COFFEE. Parana is about 77% harvested, but unusually wet conditions in some producing areas raise harvest-delay and bean-quality concerns, and a cold-air system through south-central Brazil has renewed attention on wind-related fruit losses. Parana processed coffee rose 7.7% in July to R$1,473/bag, ending a prolonged run of monthly declines.

THE c014/c015 'CONFLICT' REPORTED IN ALL FOUR EARLIER RUN LOGS TODAY DOES NOT EXIST IN THE DATA, and the series it was said to block is now charting. Every earlier log records the two AHDB winter wheat condition readings as '2026-06-29:64 and 2026-06-29:58' and as carrying conflict flags. The committed rows have event_dates 2026-05-31 and 2026-06-22, neither carries a review_flag, and c015's own quote reads 'down from 64% a month ago'. They are consecutive readings, not a contradiction. A human has since added the label, so GB|united kingdom|winter_wheat|condition_good_excellent|AHDB is chartable for the first time and the corpus now has 5 chartable series, not 4.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: FOURTH RUN OF 2026-08-09, and the second to find run_state.window_end already equal to today. Window re-covered unchanged at 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-09 (14 days); run_state was not moved. This run targeted the four sources that NONE of the three earlier runs today reached - USDA FAS World Agricultural Production, Munich Re, ECIU and FAO GIEWS - plus US livestock, which the first run named as unswept and no later run picked up.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: USDA FAS enters the corpus for the first time and it is the single largest addition of the day: the July World Agricultural Production circular cuts French corn 24 percent in one month to 10.0 Mt, the lowest since 1990/91, on yield down to 7.63 t/ha and harvested area down to 1.3 Mha, the lowest since 1969/70. USDA attributes this directly to a persistent high-pressure system bringing drought and record heat over silking and tasseling, when stress is irreversible.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: US LIVESTOCK, UNCOVERED UNTIL NOW, IS THE WORST-CONDITION CLUSTER IN THE CORPUS. USDA pasture and range for the week to 2 August has Colorado at 3 percent good-to-excellent against 76 percent very-poor-to-poor, Wyoming at 2 percent against 75 percent, and New Mexico at 5 percent against 70 percent. The 48-state good-to-excellent share is 25 percent against 44 percent a year ago. DTN reports the choice facing ranchers as herd liquidation or expensive supplemental feed.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: POSITIVE, AND FROM OFFICIAL SOURCES RATHER THAN INDIVIDUAL FARMS: seven of this run's 22 rows are favourable. USDA puts South African corn at a record 18.0 Mt on beneficial La Nina rains (yield 5.78 t/ha, fourth highest on record), Argentine corn at a record 63.0 Mt, Russian wheat yield at a record 3.53 t/ha on abundant precipitation through yield formation, and Brazilian cotton yield at a record 1,960 kg/ha after a rainy season that ran into May. South Dakota and Missouri were the only two US beef states whose pasture improved.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: KENYA IS THE WEEK'S WORST SINGLE CUT AND IT IS EL NINO-ATTRIBUTED: USDA cut Kenyan corn by a third in one month to 3.0 Mt after a prolonged dry spell from late May through June, with NDVI confirming good establishment in April and May followed by immediate crop failure in Trans Nzoia, Uasin Gishu, Bungoma and Nakuru - together roughly 37 percent of national output.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: MUNICH RE ENTERS THE CORPUS. Its 30 July half-year review independently corroborates the Indian picture the third run captured, stating the monsoon arrived late and stayed significantly weaker than normal with El Nino raising drought risk. It also supplies the attribution number behind the European crop losses: World Weather Attribution finds the recent European heatwave would have been about 3.5C cooler 50 years ago, and Germany set a national record of 41.8C at Mockern, 0.6C above the 2019 high, in June.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: A NEW FOUR-WAY DISAGREEMENT ON FRENCH MAIZE. USDA's 10.0 Mt now sits against COCERAL's 9.4 Mt (h011), RFI's 9 Mt (a022) and 8.9 Mt (j012). All four are recorded with their quotes and none is resolved; USDA is the outlier on the high side and is also the most recent official forecast rather than the most recent figure.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: FOUR SOURCES ARE SILENT FOR REASONS THE CALENDAR EXPLAINS, not because the sweep failed: the August WASDE is due 2026-08-12, the MPOB July supply and demand report is due 2026-08-10, the next USDA FAS World Agricultural Production circular is due 2026-08-12, and CONAB's next grain survey is 2026-09-15. FAO GIEWS last published its triannual Crop Prospects and Food Situation in July 2026 and is not due again within the window.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: THIRD RUN OF 2026-08-09. run_state.window_end was already today when this run started, so the window was zero-length. Rather than sweep nothing, this run re-covered 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-09 and targeted the regions the two earlier runs left thinnest — India above all, which had no rows after 2026-08-06 and whose seasonal sources (IMD, India Ministry of Agriculture) both carried last_publication: null in the manifest despite having published on 31 July and 4 August.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: IMD ENTERS THE CORPUS FOR THE FIRST TIME. Its 31 July briefing puts all-India July rainfall 1% above normal but cumulative June-July rainfall 13% below normal, with almost half of India's districts still deficient or large-deficient. August rainfall is forecast below 94% of the 254.9 mm LPA, and the August-September combined outlook is worse.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: POSITIVE, AND THE LARGEST REVERSAL OF THE SEASON: India's kharif sowing gap against last year narrowed from 25% at end-June to 2.9% by 31 July, reaching 89.42 Mha against 92.07 Mha. Rice closed to within 0.68 Mha at 30.14 Mha; sugarcane (+0.086 Mha) and oilseeds (+0.12 Mha) are ahead of last year.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: The recovery is uneven and the laggards are the ones that matter for feed and fuel: maize acreage is 0.65 Mha below last year, the steepest fall among coarse cereals, with bajra down 0.42 Mha and arhar and moong each down more than 0.3 Mha. Down To Earth notes the maize gap could tighten ethanol feedstock later in the season.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION, NOT RESOLVED HERE: Down To Earth (2026-08-05) puts end-July kharif area at 89.42 Mha; ThePrint (a032, 2026-08-06) and Reuters (j038, 2026-07-28) put it at 78.7 Mha. All three cite the same agriculture ministry series. The ~10.7 Mha gap is roughly the size of the UK's entire arable area and both readings are recorded with their quotes.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: HEAT, UNDER-COVERED UNTIL NOW: India's all-India July minimum temperature was the second highest since 1901; in the southern peninsula the July night-time temperature was the highest in 126 years. Above-normal minimums are forecast for almost all of India in August.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: A SOURCE CAVEATING ITSELF: IMD recorded 269 extremely heavy and 918 very heavy rainfall events in July, but its director general said in the same briefing that part of the rise may reflect an expanded rain-gauge network in 2026. Recorded with the caveat as a review_flag rather than as a clean year-on-year signal.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: TWO NEAR-MISSES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. Search returned an AHDB page titled 'Improved yields - winter barley and oilseed rape harvests now complete' as current; the only fetchable copy of that text is a farming.co.uk repost dated 8 August 2025, describing AHDB's third harvest 2025 report. Separately, an ADM Investor Services cocoa note surfaced as current is dated 1 June 2026. Neither was recorded. Farmers Weekly confirms the 2026 series is 'the first of four reports', so AHDB harvest report 2 is still to come and no 2026 AHDB figure beyond report 1 exists yet.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: SPAIN ENTERS THE CORPUS FOR THE FIRST TIME. Cooperativas Agro-alimentarias de España's second estimate cuts the 2026 cereal harvest to 18.6 Mt across 5.28 Mha, down 1.96 Mt (-9.5%) on the May estimate and around 30% below the exceptional 26.64 Mt of 2025; soft wheat falls 36% and barley 32%. AEMET puts the peninsular May-June temperature 3.2°C above normal with rainfall at 39% of usual.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: COCERAL's extraordinary EU crop forecast, published because of the weather, cuts EU and UK 2026 grain to 286.6 Mt, 23.4 Mt below 2025. French maize drops to 9.4 Mt from 13.8 Mt, the lowest in more than 20 years; EU+UK barley goes to 57.6 Mt and rapeseed to 21.2 Mt.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: The drought's UK effect is strikingly uneven, and that is the week's most useful finding. Against AHDB's 6.8 t/ha national wheat and the projected worst harvest since 1984, Farmers Weekly's 7 August round-up records 12 t/ha Palladium wheat and 10 t/ha malting barley on the Lincolnshire coast, 10.8 t/ha barley in North Yorkshire and 9.5 t/ha wheat in East Yorkshire — all attributed to pockets of moisture retained from early summer rainfall.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: The Environment Agency's 24-30 July report has hands-off-flow abstraction restrictions at 1,395 and national reservoir storage at 72%, 9.5% below the long-term average, with livestock farmers already eating into winter forage reserves and a straw shortage expected from short, early-cut cereals.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: Fresh produce is where the UK consumer sees it: wholesale iceberg lettuce is up more than 90% and tomatoes more than 60%, alongside the 40% potato move already in the corpus.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: Buenos Aires Grain Exchange's Argentine wheat cut — 21.3 Mt from 27.8 Mt — was the previous run's top unresolved lead and is now captured, though only from a non-mapped aggregator and with the figure verified in the headline rather than body text. It is flagged.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM THE EARLIER RUN THE SAME DAY (its 20 rows are in this count): The European Commission's 30 July balance sheet cut EU 2026/27 maize production to 51.9 Mt from 59.9 Mt in June — an 8 Mt revision that lifts the EU's maize import requirement by 5.0 Mt to 24.0 Mt — with barley also cut to 51.1 Mt.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM THE EARLIER RUN THE SAME DAY (its 20 rows are in this count): JRC MARS's July bulletin adds the ground-level detail behind the EU cuts: premature maturity and early harvesting across south-western Germany, Austria, Slovakia and Czechia; severe drought worst in Hungary; heat stress at maize flowering in northern Italy; and storm, downburst and hail lodging in northern Italy, Slovenia, Croatia and Germany.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM THE EARLIER RUN THE SAME DAY (its 20 rows are in this count): AHDB's first 2026 UK harvest report extends the poor-cereals picture to the minor crops: spring barley at 5.3 t/ha and oats at 4.9 t/ha, both below their ten-year averages, alongside the already-recorded 6.8 t/ha wheat.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM THE EARLIER RUN THE SAME DAY (its 20 rows are in this count): Ghana's COCOBOD told Reuters output will fall at least 16% in 2026/27, citing likely El Nino conditions and excessive May-June rain alongside disease and illegal mining; Ivory Coast is still expected down more than 10%, corroborating the existing July row.

CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM AN EARLIER RUN TODAY: CARRIED OVER FROM THE EARLIER RUN THE SAME DAY (its 20 rows are in this count): POSITIVE counterweight this week: Montana spring wheat jumped 12 points in good-to-excellent, US winter wheat harvest hit 86% complete, Canadian Prairie canola conditions stayed favourable, and Turkiye's cool wet spring produced record winter crop yields — enough to push Paris rapeseed futures down 6.7% to £438.99/t.

what_changed: This file now covers FIVE sweeps run on 2026-08-09 and row_count (88) is their sum: 20 + 19 + 10 + 22 + 17. Earlier content is merged forward and nothing has been overwritten. Every one of the 21 manifest sources had already been checked by one of the four earlier runs, so this run changed depth rather than coverage. Three things moved. First, the AHDB harvest report turned out to be only half mined: the four headline yields were already in, but the harvest-progress series, the 90%-of-farms distribution and the exceptional grain quality were not, and the quality finding is the corpus's first properly evidenced upside from the UK drought rather than a well-placed individual farm. Second, West African cocoa gained a third country and a mechanism: Cameroon at 247,914 t (-19.9%), against Ghana with too much rain and Cote d'Ivoire with too little sun, both flagged where the attribution is inferred rather than stated. Third, and most important for the dashboard, a claim that four consecutive run logs today asserted turns out to be false: c014 and c015 are not a same-day AHDB contradiction, they are consecutive condition readings a month apart that share a publication date. With a human-added label now in series_labels.json, that series charts, taking the corpus from 4 chartable series to 5.

conflicts.note: CORRECTION, NOT A CONFLICT. All four earlier run logs today record these as a same-day AHDB contradiction ('2026-06-29:64 and 2026-06-29:58') carrying conflict flags.
